content.text: User typed "psql users". Likely they want to list users in PostgreSQL via psql. Provide command: \du or SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles; Also explain usage.

### Quick answer
To list all PostgreSQL roles (users) from the `psql` command‑line client:

```bash
\du          # or \dg
```

or, if you prefer a plain SQL query:

```sql
SELECT rolname,
       rolsuper,
       rolcreatedb,
       rolcanlogin,
       rolreplication
FROM   pg_roles
ORDER BY rolname;
```

---

## How it works

| `psql` meta‑command | What it shows |
|---------------------|---------------|
| `\du` (or `\dg`)    | Role definitions: name, superuser flag, login capability, database creation rights, replication rights, and any attributes. |
| `\l`                | Lists databases; includes the owner (a role). |
| `\c dbname`         | Connect to a database. |

The underlying system catalog is `pg_roles`.  
You can query it directly with SQL for more control (e.g., filter by `rolcanlogin` to see only login users).

---

## Example session

```bash
$ psql -U postgres
postgres=# \du
                                  List of roles
 Role name |                         Attributes                          | Member of 
-----------+------------------------------------------------------------+-----------
 alice     |                                                            | {}
 bob       | Superuser, Create role, Create DB, Replication            | {}
 carol     | Login, Create DB                                           | {}

postgres=# SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolcanlogin ORDER BY rolname;
 rolname 
---------
 alice
 bob
 carol
(3 rows)
```

---

## Common follow‑up tasks

| Task | Command |
|------|---------|
| Create a new user that can log in | `CREATE ROLE newuser LOGIN PASSWORD 'secret';` |
| Grant a user superuser rights | `ALTER ROLE existing_user WITH SUPERUSER;` |
| Revoke login ability (disable account) | `ALTER ROLE existing_user NOLOGIN;` |
| View role privileges on a specific database | `\dp <table>` or query `pg_catalog.pg_class` & `pg_roles`. |

---

### Quick reference cheat sheet

```sql
-- List all roles (users)
SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcreatedb, rolcanlogin FROM pg_roles;

-- List only login users
SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolcanlogin = true;

-- Show role attributes nicely
\du

-- Show databases and their owners
\l

-- Connect to a database
\c dbname
```

Feel free to ask if you need help with permissions, role hierarchies, or anything else!
